title: Pi as an unattended worker: verify it live and give it a real full-auto template
description:
Pi is reachable as a herdr kind but is NOT verified for unattended work, so any
role routed to it starts without a full-auto template and can stall on a
permission prompt. Pi supports unattended operation; nobody has established HOW
under herdr, and the kinds table says so honestly rather than guessing.

Verified 2026-09-10 by exercising the real validator (Compile with kind "pi"):

- A provider-qualified Cloudflare id compiles and produces
  `--model cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3:high`. Effort is a SUFFIX
  for pi (effortStyleSuffix), not a flag.
- Every compile emits: `kind "pi" has no verified full-auto template in
  herdr-kinds.md; starting without one.` It is a WARNING, not a refusal, so a
  run starts and may simply hang.
- `internal/herd/config/kinds.go` pi row: fullAuto nil, fullAutoVerified false,
  modelFlag `--model`, effortFlag `--thinking`, efforts off..max, modelOK
  providerQualified. Its comment records that the row was read from `pi --help`
  only.
- Local Pi is 0.85.1. `pi auth check --provider cloudflare-workers-ai` reports
  ready with an api_key, and `pi --list-models` lists 18 cloudflare-workers-ai
  models, so the provider side is genuinely set up.

Do:
1. Find pi's real unattended story from `pi --help` and its docs — the flag or
   config that suppresses approval prompts, whatever it is called. Do not
   transcribe another kind's shape.
2. Round-trip it live, following herdr-kinds.md "Adding a kind" exactly: create
   a WORKSPACE (never `pane split --current`, which resolves to whatever the
   operator is looking at), `herdr agent start` with the candidate template,
   confirm the ECHOED argv, prompt with `--wait`, read the pane for the answer,
   record `herdr agent get` and the `agent_session`.
3. Verify resume: C-c (not `ctrl-c`, which errors `unsupported key`), restart in
   the same pane with a FRESH agent name, confirm the prior turn is present.
4. Record the integration state (`herdr integration status`), since the wave
   loop depends on lifecycle states.
5. Clean up every pane and workspace created.
6. Then set fullAuto and fullAutoVerified in the pi row, and write the pi
   section of herdr-kinds.md from what you actually ran.

Also fix, found alongside:
- `providerQualified` (kinds.go:306) only checks for a slash ANYWHERE, so a bare
  Cloudflare id like `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3` passes while naming no provider, and
  would reach pi unqualified. Tighten it, or say why the loose check is right.
- Pi's catalog marks which models support thinking. Several cloudflare entries
  do not, and the effort suffix is appended unconditionally, so an economy tier
  on a non-thinking model likely fails at launch. Decide whether that is a
  compile-time refusal (opencode's precedent, kinds.go, treats a missing effort
  dimension as a refusal rather than a silent drop) or a documented constraint.

Placement: the capability matrix is EXECUTION config, so it is ticfac's under
Phase 2 — which is why this tick lives here and not in the ticks tracker. It is
blocked behind the config split (wgi) because the pi row belongs beside the
roles and tiers tables once those are ticfac's. The live round-trip itself can
be done against the current ticks code at any time; what must land here is the
verified template, in ticfac.

Sources to read first, both in the ticks repo today:
`internal/herd/config/kinds.go` (the matrix and its validators) and
`skills/ticks/references/herdr-kinds.md` ("Adding a kind", the green-start trap,
and the operational notes that bit during the opencode round trip).

Two of those notes will bite here: verify the CLI is on the INTERACTIVE shell's
PATH (`zsh -i -c 'which pi'`), because herdr starts the agent in a pane at an
interactive prompt; and `herdr agent prompt --wait` without `--until` matches
idle|done|blocked and does not track turns, so an already-working agent's
current turn can satisfy the wait.
acceptance_criteria: The pi row in ticfac's capability matrix carries a full-auto template that was round-tripped LIVE, with its verified flag set, and the pi section of the kinds reference is written from the actual run: echoed argv, agent_session, resume confirmed after a C-c restart under a fresh agent name, integration state recorded. A pi worker dispatched for a real tick completes an unattended turn without stalling on a permission prompt, and the run is shown end to end. A model id that names no provider (a bare cloudflare id such as @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3) is refused, or the doc states why the loose check is correct. An effort level on a model whose catalog entry has no thinking dimension is refused at compile time or documented as a constraint, matching the opencode precedent that a missing effort dimension is a refusal rather than a silent drop. Every pane and workspace created during verification is cleaned up. go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
